statement.excerpt: OpenAI’s lobbying campaign, simply put, is based on a false dichotomy (give everything to us free or we will die)—and also a threat: either we get to use all the existing IP we want for free, or you won’t get to generative AI anymore.
statement.document_title: The desperate race to save Generative AI

from_speaker: all the existing IP we want for free

our_interpretation: The testable proposition is that the lobbying campaign invoked in the post presented unrestricted, unpaid access as necessary for continued generative AI availability while excluding licensing alternatives.
The target is the latest UK lobbying episode discussed in the post, through 2024-01-08. Its starting date is not specified.
A claim that competitive models require copyrighted material does not by itself establish a claim that the material must be free.
Calling the argument a threat is an interpretation of its implications, not necessarily a claim that OpenAI used those exact words.
criteria.support_condition: The relevant statements make continued generative AI availability depend on unpaid access to copyrighted material and exclude licensing as a practical alternative.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The relevant statements expressly acknowledge licensing alternatives and make a narrower claim about training competitive models, without the alleged free-access-or-disappearance choice.
